contexts.text: There, historical things are given to oblivion. AC 7112:2.
(Until) he forget that which thou hast done to him () = habit from delay. To forget, here, = the successful abolition of repugnance.

But forgat him () = removal. When not to remember = no conjunction, to forget removal, because in proportion as there is no conjunction there is removal. That which is given to oblivion is also removed.

All the plenty shall be given to oblivion in the land of Egypt () = the removal of truth, and its apparent privation in each Natural. To forget or be given to oblivion = removal and consequent apparent deprivation... (For) the things of which a, man is thinking are immediately under his view, and the things which relate to them present themselves in order round about, even to the things not in relation and which are most remote, and which are therefore in oblivion.
God hath made me forget all my toil () = the removal (of evils) after temptations.
In the Original Language, Manasseh means forgetfulness; thus, in the internal sense, removal, namely, of evils both actual and hereditary; for when these have been removed the new Voluntary rises.
By the Divine remembrance is signified salvation; and by no remembrance, or oblivion, damnation.
In the case of beasts and birds, (there is) a total forgetfulness of relationship.
As he descended, forgetfulness drove away recollection.
They are then in forgetfulness, that is, in no thought about His Divine.
The evils from which is their worship are signified by, My people hath forgotten Me (); for he who forgets God is in evils.
Therefore have they forgotten Me () = that pride has obliterated these things; and thus their longing, and with this their heart, has departed from the Lord.
